data.hypothesis: The valid 128-thread/128-source-tile parent is faster than the measured 256-thread/256-source-tile candidate, but those measurements change both CTA and tile size. This candidate keeps the 128-source tile and its 2048-byte shared-memory footprint while using 256 target threads per CTA. The wider CTA may increase source reuse and reduce CTA count, though occupancy or scheduling effects could offset that; official timing must decide.

memory_lessons.applicability: These measurements are from this campaign and do not isolate tile width from CTA width.
memory_lessons.claim: The valid 128-thread/128-source-tile candidate measured 0.0008998 seconds, while the valid compact 256-thread/256-source-tile candidate measured 0.0010112 seconds. This comparison alone does not establish which configuration factor explains the difference.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Hold source tile width and shared-memory allocation at 128 entries/2048 bytes, and measure a 256-thread CTA.

data.notes: This is a source proposal only; correctness and performance have not been measured. Every thread reaches both barriers, including inactive target threads and threads outside the 128-entry loading range. Valid targets exclude self-interaction and write once.
transformations: Use a 256-thread CTA and matching 256-item launch mapping for complete target coverage.
Keep a fixed 128-source compact shared-memory tile, cooperatively loaded by the first 128 threads, with 2048 bytes of dynamic shared memory.

Retain one target and force accumulator per active thread; all threads participate in both barriers, partial source tiles are bounded, self-interactions are excluded by global index, and each valid target is written once.
